neighborhoods_visited: Sun Valley Village / Trail Creek / Dollar Mountain
guide_description: One day covering the historic core of America's first destination ski resort: the Sun Valley Lodge and its surrounding village, the Trail Creek corridor where Hemingway wrote and hunted, and the open slopes of Dollar Mountain. The cluster is compact and walkable, mixing mid-century resort architecture with genuine mountain landscape.

days.cluster_name: Sun Valley Village and Trail Creek
days.cluster_tagline: America's first destination ski resort - 1930s lodge glamour, Hemingway country, and open mountain terrain
days.neighborhood_focus: Sun Valley Village / Trail Creek / Dollar Mountain
days.neighborhood_description: Sun Valley was built from scratch in 1936 by Union Pacific Railroad as a destination resort modeled on European Alpine villages. The compact village sits at roughly 1,750 meters elevation in the Wood River Valley in central Idaho, with the Sun Valley Lodge as its social anchor and Trail Creek running just east through sagebrush and cottonwood terrain that became inseparable from Ernest Hemingway's Idaho years.

morning.notes: The main lobby and Ram Restaurant corridor are lined with black-and-white photographs of every celebrity who stayed here from the 1930s onward - Gary Cooper, Clark Gable, Marilyn Monroe, and a recurring Hemingway. Walk the ground floor hallways without paying for a room; the outdoor ice rink immediately in front of the lodge was operating year-round before artificial rinks were common anywhere in America, and the heated outdoor pool is visually unchanged from the 1936 opening photographs.

afternoon.notes: The log cabin one mile east of the lodge along Trail Creek Road was Hemingway's preferred lunch and dinner spot during his repeated Idaho stays from 1939 onward. He completed For Whom the Bell Tolls nearby and is buried in the Ketchum Cemetery a short drive south. The walk along the creek from the lodge follows a well-worn path through cottonwoods and open meadow; in summer the creek is audible the entire route. The cabin still operates as a restaurant in winter, more limited in summer - call ahead before treating it as a dining stop.

evening.notes: The smaller of Sun Valley's two ski mountains sits directly north of the village and was the original learning hill when the resort opened in 1936. Outside ski season the chairlift is not operational, but the lower slopes and base area give an unobstructed view south down the Wood River Valley at golden hour, with the Pioneer Mountains visible to the southeast. The light on the sage-covered hillsides turns amber about forty minutes before official sunset - the valley floor is narrow enough that the sun drops behind the western ridge well before astronomical sunset.

if_time_permits.notes: A simple bronze bust of Hemingway set beside Trail Creek about two miles south of Sun Valley Village in Ketchum, with a quote from his eulogy for a fellow hunter. The site is on a short paved path along the creek bank and takes ten minutes to reach on foot from the Ketchum town center or five minutes by car from Sun Valley. The Ketchum Cemetery where Hemingway and his wife Mary are buried is an additional quarter mile south - both stops together take under an hour.

The outdoor amphitheater adjacent to the Lodge has hosted the Sun Valley Summer Symphony since 1984, with the stage backed by Dollar Mountain. Even outside performance season the open-air shell and lawn seating area are worth a look as an intact piece of mid-century resort landscape design. Check the symphony schedule if your visit falls between late July and mid-August - lawn tickets are inexpensive and the acoustics across the open grass are surprisingly good.
